videos.script: Courses and study sessions have little in common. A planner still wants to show both in one list. {{protocol}} A protocol is how Swift says what a family of types promises, and nothing about how. You will write one, and watch the compiler refuse a type that forgot a requirement. {{extension}} Then extensions. They add behaviour to a type you did not write, even an Int, and never storage. {{default}} An extension of a protocol gives every conforming type a default. Write your own, and yours wins. {{standard}} Then four protocols the standard library already has. The compiler writes equality and hashing for you. {{dispatch}} And one surprise. The same call, on the same value, runs two different bodies. You will see why, and the one habit that prevents it.
